{{Short description|Mathematics concept}}
The '''Andronov&ndash;Pontryagin criterion''' is a necessary and sufficient condition for the stability of [[dynamical system]]s in the plane. It was derived by [[Aleksandr Andronov]] and [[Lev Pontryagin]] in 1937.

==Statement==

A dynamical system

: <math>\dot{x} = v(x), </math>

where <math>v</math> is a <math>C^{1}</math>-[[vector field]] on the [[Euclidean plane|plane]], <math>x \in \mathbb{R}^{2}</math>, 
is [[topological conjugacy|orbitally topologically stable]] if and only if the following two conditions hold:

# All [[equilibrium point]]s and [[periodic orbit]]s are ''hyperbolic''.
# There are no ''saddle connections''.

The same statement holds if the vector field <math>v</math> is defined on the [[unit disk]] and is transversal to the boundary.

==Clarifications==

'''Orbital topological stability''' of a dynamical system means that for any sufficiently small perturbation (in the ''C''<sup>1</sup>-metric), there exists a [[homeomorphism]] close to the identity map which transforms the orbits of the original dynamical system to the orbits of the perturbed system (cf [[structural stability]]).

The first condition of the theorem is known as '''global hyperbolicity'''.  A zero of a vector field ''v'', i.e. a point ''x''<sub>0</sub> where ''v''(''x''<sub>0</sub>)=0, is said to be '''hyperbolic''' if none of the [[eigenvalue]]s of the linearization of ''v'' at ''x''<sub>0</sub> is purely imaginary. A periodic orbit of a flow is said to be hyperbolic if none of the [[eigenvalue]]s of the [[Poincaré map|Poincaré return map]] at a point on the orbit has absolute value one.

Finally, '''saddle connection''' refers to a situation where an orbit from one saddle point enters the same or another saddle point, i.e. the unstable and stable [[separatrix (mathematics)|separatrices]] are connected (cf [[homoclinic orbit]] and [[heteroclinic orbit]]).
